text:
raj: FYI ran a customer incident this morning. Premium customers in us-west got routed to a quantized variant during regional pressure and p95 spiked to ~420ms (target 150ms).
michelle: yikes. what triggered the handoff? queue backlog or node OOMs?
raj: queue_depth + degraded node availability. Our router looked only at compatibility and pool capacity, not tier SLOs. We need SLO-first routing CBs.
dan: high-level mapping idea: account-tier SLOs -> routing policy -> CB thresholds. For premium, prefer variants with historical p95 < SLO and only fall back when CB opens.
eva: agree but watch for oscillation. If CB windows are too short we'll thrash between variants.
oliver: suggested design: two-phase decision path:
oliver: 1) fast admission: evaluate candidate variant's recent p95 and KV-cache hit rate; if likely to meet SLO allow, else skip to fallback list or region failover.
oliver: 2) variant-level circuit-breaker: inputs = p95_latency, error_rate, queue_depth; CBs open with exponential backoff and emit events.
michelle: also enforce cost_budgets/quotas so premium traffic doesn't automatically go to the most expensive top-tier variant. Need cost_multiplier or budget cap.
raj: agreed. policy should include: latency target, availability target, ordered fallbacks, and cost guardrails.
eva: draft policy example (for discussion):
raj: ```yaml
routing_policy:
  account: acme-corp
  tier: premium
  slo:
    latency_p95_ms: 150
    availability_pct: 99.95
  fallbacks:
    - variant: hero-8q
      max_extra_latency_ms: 60
      allowed_cost_multiplier: 0.8
    - variant: hero-amt
      max_extra_latency_ms: 120
      allowed_cost_multiplier: 1.2
  circuit_breaker:
    signals: ["latency_p95_ms","error_rate","queue_depth"]
    latency_multiplier: 1.25  # open if p95 > slo * multiplier
    absolute_latency_open_ms: 250  # absolute floor
    error_rate_threshold: 0.015
    sample_window_sec: 45
    open_base_sec: 15
    backoff_mult: 2
```
sre-bot: alert: us-west variant pool saturated 03:12 UTC, autoscale +3 nodes triggered
michelle: notes: latency_multiplier is convenient but include absolute thresholds for small SLOs. sample_window_sec needs tuning per-region.
dan: telemetry work: we need per (account_tier, variant, region, route) histograms for p50/p95/p99 and queue_depth gauges. Use EWMA for error_rate to reduce noise.
eva: console UX idea: simulation tool that replays last 7 days and shows how many requests would have fallen back, estimated p95 change, and cost delta. Include a toggle to simulate cross-region failover.
oliver: API question: attach policies at account level or route level? If account-level default + route overrides, we get sane inheritance.
raj: leaning account defaults with route overrides. Most customers want a default SLO but some routes (e.g., embeddings) may need different SLOs.
michelle: rollout plan: feature-flag enforcement server-side, read-only display in console initially, then editing behind enterprise RBAC after 2 weeks.
dan: API shapes: PATCH /accounts/:id/routing_policy and POST /simulate/routing_policy with time range, return simulated fallback counts and cost estimate.
eva: metric naming: redwood.routing.{region}.{variant}.{tier}.latency.p95_ms and emit CB events: redwood.routing.cb_event with fields variant, region, trigger, measured, slo.
oliver: when CB opens emit event with reason and open_until timestamp. Console should show active CBs and recent opens/closes.
raj: ops question: on CB open do we immediately failover to existing region variant, or try autoscale first? Suggest conservative: attempt adjacent-region failover if latency budget allows, else let autoscale complete then retry. Must respect data residency flags.
michelle: add cooldown to avoid rapid cross-region flip-flops; failover must check account residency constraint and capacity.
raj: action items:
raj: - dan: add p95 histograms and EWMA error_rate per (tier, variant, region). due EOD Wed.
raj: - oliver: implement CB operator prototype with exponential backoff + event emission. due Fri.
raj: - michelle: console simulation mock + docs for policy schema. due next Tue.
raj: - eva: add PATCH policy and POST simulate endpoints + RBAC scopes. due next Wed.
raj: tagging @oncall @infra for visibility :eyes: 
slo-bot: policy-proposal posted for acct=acme-corp; sim results: est p95 improvement 0.9%, est cost delta +3%
deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2145601200 -> eng-platform-canary
michelle: keep the policy primitives minimal. small DSL, good defaults, strong telemetry and sim coverage.
raj: I'll open RFC + JSON schema + simulation harness PR tonight.
